prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-04-23. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.35 |
| Retained earnings       | 26,088M |
| Current liabilities     | 159,640M |
| Current assets          | 56,524M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 33,995M |
| Total liabilities       | 274,899M |
| Total assets            | 308,894M |
| EBIT / operating income | 6,598M |
| Revenue                 | 20,880M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-04-23, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported current ratio of 0.35 signals acute liquidity stress, with negative working capital exceeding one-third of total assets. Combined with high leverage (equity only ~11% of assets) this produces an Altman Z-score well below the distress threshold. Modest positive EBIT and retained earnings prevent an immediate “C” classification but are insufficient to support an investment-grade or even high-yield rating.
DECISION: CCC
(The rating reflects only the static 2026-04-23 balance-sheet snapshot and pre-2026 rating conventions; forward-looking factors are ignored.)
